REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - OCTOBER 26, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 3-0, with two Commissioners absent, to approve the following:
Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP 84298, A PROPOSAL BY CERRITOS-2 DEVELOPMENT LLC, TO SUBDIVIDE ONE (1) EXISTING PARCEL INTO TWO (2) SEPARATE PARCELS. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS LOCATED AT 13730 ARTESIA BOULEVARD, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703, AND IS ZONED SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL (RS-6500) (APN 7022-005-031) (COUNCIL).*
Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING PRECISE PLAN 2023-15, A PROPOSAL BY CERRITOS-2 DEVELOPMENT LLC, TO CONSTRUCT A NEW SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT COMPRISED OF TWO (2) LOTS, ONE (1) WITH A NEW TWO-STORY RESIDENCE (PARCEL 1), AND ONE (1) WITH A NEW ONE-STORY RESIDENCE AND A DETACHED ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT (ADU) LOCATED IN THE REAR YARD (PARCEL 2). ADDITIONAL IMPROVEMENTS INCLUDE NEW SIDEWALKS, PARKWAY LANDSCAPING, AND OTHER RELATED SITE IMPROVEMENTS. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS LOCATED AT 13730 ARTESIA BOULEVARD, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703, AND IS ZONED SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL (RS-6500) (APN 7022-005-031) (COUNCIL).*
*The applicant has proposed a detached accessory dwelling unit (ADU) on Parcel 2 of Tentative Parcel Map 84298. In accordance with state planning and zoning laws, and with concurrence by the applicant, the public hearing will not apply to the proposed ADU, which will be processed administratively by City staff after completion of review for the new single-family housing development pursuant to Tentative Parcel Map 84298 and Precise Plan 2023-15.

Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, OCTOBER 26,
2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Tina Tribolet, New Life Community Church.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Troop 529.

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

 5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Ellen Rodriguez-Swing, President of the Filipino American Chamber of Commerce of
  Cerritos, Lee Natividad, Vice Chair of the Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce, and
  Kaitlin Casica, President of Cerritos High School Club Magkaisa (Filipino American History
  Month).

 5B.  City Council recognition of City Manager Art Gallucci’s final Cerritos City Council meeting.

  A proclamation was presented by the City Council to retiring City Manager Art Gallucci in honor
  and recognition of his fifty-two years of service to the City of Cerritos. A proclamation was
  also presented from Assemblymember Sharon Quirk-Silva by Joe Pak, Field
  Representative.

 5C.  Review and consideration of appointments, removals, and filling of scheduled or unscheduled
  vacancies on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (2022-24 term) (COUNCIL).

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to approve Mayor Barrows’
  nomination, as listed below, to fill an unscheduled vacancy of an unexpired two-year term
  of service expiring April 30, 2024 (COUNCIL):

  Nominee Name  Advisory Board
  Lew Gentiluomo  Property Preservation Commission
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 26, 2023, 7:00 p.m.

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5C.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer, administered the oath of office to newly appointed
  Property Preservation Commissioner Lew Gentiluomo.

5D.  Review and consideration of appointment to the Board of Trustees of the Greater Los
  Angeles County Vector Control District (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Reappoint the current eligible incumbent, Mark Bollman, to a four (4) year term on the
  Board of Trustees of the Greater Los Angeles Vector Control District (District); and

  2. Direct the City Clerk/Treasurer to notify the District of the City Council appointment
  prior to January 1, 2024, as stipulated in the State Health and Safety Code (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Katarina Thompson requested traffic calming measures in the Granada Park neighborhood
  and requested the City assign a staff liaison to work with the neighborhood’s residents.

  Samar Malouf requested traffic calming measures in the Granada Park neighborhood and
  requested the City assign a staff liaison to work with the neighborhood’s residents.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum acknowledged the upcoming holiday season and expressed concern
  with traffic impacts at certain intersections within the City.

  Teddy Lloyd expressed gratitude to the City for repairing streetlights near the Cerritos
  Sports Complex, inquired as to methods for reporting such concerns to the City, and
  whether residents could receive approximate timelines for when reported concerns would
  be addressed or completed.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 26, 2023, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Mark Pulido expressed gratitude for the City’s recognition of Filipino American History
  Month and offered his heartfelt acknowledgment of City Manager Art Gallucci’s significant
  contributions to the City of Cerritos.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Thursday, October 12, 2023, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting

  In-Person Comments:

  Pavan Maddi, applicant, commented that his submitted design for the subject proposed

  construction of the proposed subject project can be accomplished via Artesia Boulevard.

  Derjane “Jennifer” Shih expressed concerns regarding the potential parking and other
  negative impacts of the subject proposed project.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor

9.  New and Old Business

9B.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS DIRECTING THAT THE OUTSTANDING ENTERPRISE

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Finance Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2023-35, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS DIRECTING THAT THE
  OUTSTANDING ENTERPRISE FUND LOAN BALANCES OWED BY THE WATER AND
  SEWER FUNDS TO THE GENERAL FUND BE WRITTEN OFF AND FURTHER
  DIRECTING THAT ANY FUTURE FUNDING PROVIDED BY THE GENERAL FUND TO
  THE WATER AND/OR SEWER FUNDS BE CLASSIFIED AS A NON-REIMBURSABLE

  related to current sewer services provided to the City by the Los Angeles County

  of adjustments to City sewer rates; and
